A.  COYOTE MANAGEMENT

  Recommendation: That the City Council receive and file the report on the current
  Coyote Management Program and direct staff to coordinate a Peninsula-wide
  community education workshop in coordination with partnering agencies to further
  implement education strategies.

  Assistant to the City Manager Davis provided a staff report outlining the City’s current
  Coyote Management Program (as per agenda materials).

  Niamh Quinn, Ph.D., Human Wildlife Interaction Advisor, University of California
  Cooperative Extension provided an overview of coyote biology and ecology.

  Deputy Jim Hartman, Pest Management Division Head, Los Angeles County
  Agricultural Commissioner/Weights & Measures provided an overview of the County’s
  coyote management program and the support the County provides to the City.

  Dave Dodge, Volunteer, Wildlife Watch Program, California Department of Fish &
  Wildlife provided an overview of the Wildlife Watch Program, its successes and how the
  program is being implemented locally. Mr. Dodge expressed the importance of
  neighborhood involvement.

  In response to Councilmember Mitchell, Deputy Hartman commented that a resident
  may not discharge a firearm in the City to kill a coyote; and if a resident wanted to
  trap a coyote, they would be required to obtain the applicable licensing and permits.

  Also in response to Councilmember Mitchell, Assistant to the City Manager Davis
  commented that the City is aware of one private trapping firm and staff shares the
  contact information for that firm with interested residents when asked.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
NOVEMBER 28, 2017
   MAYOR ZERUNYAN explained the process for taking public comment and stated that
  the City Council is interested in hearing from all parties on this matter so that sound
  policy decisions can be made to address the coyote issue. He then called for comments
  from the public.

  The following residents addressed the City Council to express concern regarding
  aggressive coyotes and urge the City to do more to manage coyotes in the community:
  Cindy Martin, Daniel Schuch, Lisa Turek, Tim Scott. Jim Gardner, Matt Whitcomb
  and Sue Martin.

  The following residents addressed the City Council to express concern regarding
  coyotes and share strategies that they have found helpful in dealing with coyotes: Cat
  Spydell and Tony Trutanich.

  In response to the questions raised during public comment, staff and the experts
  present provided further explanation with regard to the average number of pups born
  in a pack, the feeding habits of coyotes, the costs associated with County services and
  additional strategies for safeguarding properties and pets against coyotes.

  MAYOR ZERUNYAN commented that the City has a very comprehensive coyote
  management program; but addressing this issue requires collaboration between the
  city, its citizens and other sectors, including the neighboring communities.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN commented that some policy options the City may
  consider include review of the threshold for determining when coyotes pose a threat;
  using locking trashcans on public property and addressing issues raised by residents
  feeding pets/wildlife through code enforcement. He further suggested residents may
  consider using velcro as a means to secure trashcan lids.

  In response to COUNCILMEMBER MITCHELL regarding the coyote management
  resources available from the City including the Coyote Management Program
  document, Assistant to the City Manager Davis commented that all of the resources
  are on the City’s website under Public Safety and shared/disseminated at various
  community meetings. COUNCILMEMBER MITCHELL further commented that hosting
  a community meeting on this topic would be very useful for residents. She also
  suggested developing a system for tracking the location of the coyotes and working
  with the golf course to address coyote issues.

  COUNICLMEMBER SCHMITZ commented that she also believes that hosting a
  community workshop on this topic would be very useful for residents and suggested
  that education regarding feeding wildlife be part of the program.

  In response to MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF regarding the concern a member of the public
  raised regarding the County’s response time in setting traps, Mr. Hartman stated that
  the County always attempts to respond in a timely manner, but sometimes there are
  extenuating factors that could cause a delay.

  City Manager Prichard commented that as the City Council moves forward in
  discussing policies related to coyote management, some items it may wish to consider
  are whether or not to allow trapping on public property and adjusting the escalation
  point for the lethal removal of coyotes and budget needs.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
NOVEMBER 28, 2017
   In response to MAYOR ZERUNYAN’s suggestion that a packet containing effective
  hazing tactics be made available to residents, Mr. Dodge reviewed hazing techniques
  and suggest items that could be included in an information packet.

  Also in response to MAYOR ZERUNYAN, Dr. Quinn stated that the only population
  control option for coyotes is sterilization and it is not a feasible option. With regard to
  tracking coyote encounters, Dr. Quinn noted that there is a program called Coyote
  Cacher designed to track coyote encounters. Assistant City Manager Davis noted that
  the City of Rancho Palos Verdes also developed a program for the peninsula cities
  residents to report coyote sightings.

  Further discussion ensued regarding the options for moving forward toward adopting
  policy to address the coyote issue.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ

  TO RECEIVE AND FILE THE COYOTE MANAGEMENT REPORT AND DIRECT
  STAFF TO COORDINATE A PENINSULA-WIDE COMMUNITY EDUCATION
  WORKSHOP IN CONJUNCTION WITH PARTNERING AGENCIES TO FURTHER
  IMPLEMENT EDUCATION STRATEGIES.

  STAFF WAS FURTHER DIRECTED TO AGENDIZE THE MATTER FOR
  DISCUSSION AT THE 2018 POLICY DEVELOPMENT SESSION.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

B.  SPECIAL PARK & ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF NOVEMBER 20, 2017

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ.

  TO RECEIVE AND FILE SPECIAL PARK & ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES
  OF NOVEMBER 20, 2017.

NOVEMBER 28, 2017
 10.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  BID RESULTS – STORM DRAIN REHABILITATION PROJECT

  Recommendation: That the City Council reject all bids and authorize staff to re-
  advertise with a revised bid package for the 2017-19 Storm Drain Rehabilitation
  Project.

  Assistant City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

  In response to COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN, Assistant City Manager Grammer
  stated that there was ambiguity in the answers that were provided to a question that
  arose during the bid process causing the wide discrepancy in the bid results.

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ.

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL REJECT ALL BIDS AND AUTHORIZE STAFF TO RE-
  ADVERTISE WITH A REVISED BID PACKAGE FOR THE 2017-18 STORM
  DRAIN REHABILITATION PROJECT.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

 OTHER REPORTS:

COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL reported that the Palos Verdes Peninsula Chamber of
Commerce is again attempting to hold a “Wine Walk” at Peninsula Center – tentatively
scheduled for March, 2018.

COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL reported that the SCAQMD has activated its “CHECK
BEFORE YOU BURN” policy between November 1, 2018 and February 28, 2018 and provided
information on how residents can determine whether or not burning wood is allowed.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ thanked MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF for her efforts in convincing
the SBCCOG to consider the dues formula matter sooner rather than later.

COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN congratulated COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL on her
reappointment to the AQMD Board.

COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ reminded the City Council and those present that the City’s
Parade of Lights is this Saturday, December 2 and the Nutcracker is also playing at the
Norris Theater over the weekend with several shows over the course of the weekend.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN expressed continued concern regarding stormwater
regulation and the City Council inquired as to the status of the City of Gardena’s lawsuit
regarding the matter.
